bug_semantics: A local attacker can make an AutoOpts consumer such as tcpliveplay process a missing, inaccessible, empty, wrong-type, or malformed option file via --load-opts. optionProcess() then reaches optionSaveFile(), whose update/rewrite path calls open_sv_file() and remove_settings(). Vulnerable remove_settings() passes text_mmap()'s unchecked MAP_FAILED result to strstr(); the optimized libc __strstr_sse2 implementation consequently reads from an invalid address near -1 and aborts, producing the reported denial of service. The same routine also assumed successful mappings were NUL-terminated even though text_mmap() documented only a best-effort terminator, creating a related out-of-bounds scan risk.
flaw_origin: Commit a3890282a571bf1754fa20dc325906f05ce70597 upgraded the vendored runtime to AutoGen/libopts 5.18.16 and, for the first time in this repository, added libopts/save.c::remove_settings() plus the update-mode call from open_sv_file(). The new function assigned text_mmap() directly to text/scan and called strstr(scan, zCfgProg) without the failure guard already used by the other text_mmap() callers. Its direct parent 76644c24abde01dcf7f746bb3432b0dcf0b1838a had no remove_settings(), no text_mmap(fname, ...) call, and no strstr(scan, zCfgProg) scan; open_sv_file() instead replaced the file through the older write-mode path. Thus this is new vulnerable behavior rather than a move or refactor of pre-existing vulnerable lines.

reasoning: Field reconciliation 2026-08-29 (see evidence tail). The reported crash is not a defect in glibc's SIMD strstr implementation: that function is the first consumer to expose an invalid pointer supplied by vendored libopts. At 6fcbf0324088561d95c356fe8337f4faac275f1a, --load-opts can cause optionProcess() to invoke the option-file save/rewrite path, and remove_settings() trusts text_mmap() even though the mapper explicitly returns MAP_FAILED on failure. The smallest commit in the assigned repository that creates the causal chain is a3890282a571bf1754fa20dc325906f05ce70597: it adds both the vulnerable remove_settings() code and its update-mode caller. Its direct parent has neither the function nor any of the three identifying vulnerable expressions, proving absence rather than relying on blame. The commit is a single logical vendored-version upgrade commit/PR, not a squash merge with reconstructable member commits, and the parent used a materially different replace-by-write behavior, so no move/revert/refactor is being mistaken for the BIC. Tag ancestry puts the BIC after v4.4.2 and first in v4.4.3. Commit abca92c57d4dd24dd2c0768567551d43a09de6dd closes the exact MAP_FAILED-to-strstr path and is first released in v4.5.4, consistent with the later first-party repository advisory and release notes; the parallel v4.6 branch has the stronger b50828c575d0840e5c505f6ab6089d7ab500dea3 remediation. Finally, the complete BIC commit object has a human author and committer and no AI marker. Under the protocol's BIC-only attribution rule, later AI-assisted fixes are irrelevant, so the causal verdict is NOT_AI.
